marble.name: Dividing by two-digit numbers
marble.subject: Mathematics
marble.description: Divide numbers up to 4 digits by a two-digit number using formal written short division where appropriate, interpreting remainders according to context
marble.prompt: Can you use short division to work out something like '2,184 ÷ 12' — keeping track of each digit and carrying any remainders into the next column?

cluster.summary: Your child is being introduced to multiplication and division as ways of working with equal groups — understanding multiplication as repeated addition and division as sharing equally.

misconceptions: Forcing short division with an awkward divisor and making mental-multiple errors (should choose long division).
Carry/remainder errors in the compressed steps because the mental multiplication is insecure.
Not interpreting the remainder appropriately for the context.
Believing one method is always 'better' rather than choosing by the numbers.
Place-value slips when the divisor doesn't fit into a leading digit.
representations: Short-division ('bus stop') layout with a 2-digit divisor
Side-by-side short vs long division of the same calculation (efficiency comparison)
Divisor multiples list to support the mental steps
Bar model / number line for remainder interpretation
authoredAnswer: 3,648 ÷ 16 = 228 (exact). For 5 m ÷ 16, each piece is 0.3125 m (or 5/16 m). The teacher watches for a workable division method (chunking known multiples of 16, or short/long division) and correct interpretation of the remainder as a fraction/decimal rather than 'r something' when the context demands it.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: child cannot start, or writes quotient digits with no relation to multiples of 16
wrongAnswers.fix: build a short menu of easy multiples first (16, 32, 160, 1600) and subtract chunks; a two-digit divisor needs known multiples, not a memorised table.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: answer given as '0 m r5' or similar rather than 5/16 m or 0.3125 m
wrongAnswers.fix: ask 'what does the leftover mean when we're sharing metres?' — the remainder over the divisor is a fraction of a piece; convert to decimal for length.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: quotient has the wrong number of digits; e.g. drops a place when 16 won't divide a leading part
wrongAnswers.fix: insist on writing a zero in the quotient when the divisor doesn't fit that place, carrying the amount on; check the quotient's magnitude by estimation.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: one step wrong; estimate (3600÷16 ≈ 225) flags it
wrongAnswers.fix: do not reteach; have the child check with multiplication (228×16 = 3648?) and estimate.
